Separately, the Congressional Budget Office reported the Iran war has cost $38 billion with projected ongoing monthly expenses of $2–3 billion. New images obtained by CBS News document widespread damage at U.S. military bases in the Middle East from Iranian missile and drone strikes.

claims.statement: The U.S. House passed a war powers resolution to limit President Trump's military authority against Iran.
Seven Republicans voted in favor of the war powers resolution alongside Democrats.
This is the third time the House has voted on such a war powers resolution regarding Iran.
The House passed the war powers resolution by a vote of 220-204.
The CBO projects the U.S. will spend at least $2 billion per month on the Iran war going forward.
The United States has spent $38 billion on the Iran war, according to the Congressional Budget Office.
A presidential veto of the war powers resolution is all but certain.
The war powers resolution was sponsored by Rep. Seth Moulton (D-Mass.).
Iran conducted missile and drone strikes against U.S. bases in the Middle East.
Public opposition to military action in Iran is growing ahead of the midterm elections.
Previous House votes on Iran war powers resolutions failed to stop President Trump from waging war with Iran.
New images obtained exclusively by CBS News show widespread damage across U.S. bases in the Middle East from Iranian strikes.
The images documenting damage at U.S. bases were provided to CBS News by active service members under condition of anonymity.
The war powers resolution limits Trump's military engagement in Iran beyond a 60-day threshold without congressional approval.
Previous House votes on Iran war powers resolutions had four Republican supporters; this vote had seven, three more than before.
Republicans who voted for the resolution include Reps. Thomas Massie (Ky.), Brian Fitzpatrick (Pa.), Warren Davidson (Ohio), Tom Barrett (Mich.), and Mariannette Miller-Meeks.

context.significance: The repeated House votes on Iran war powers — now three times — echo the pattern of congressional struggles during Vietnam and the post-9/11 era to reassert authority over executive military commitments that expand faster than legislative oversight can respond. The CBO's $38 billion figure and multi-billion monthly burn rate place the Iran conflict among the most expensive U.S. military operations in recent decades, with compounding fiscal consequences that extend well beyond the immediate military campaign. Growing Republican defections signal a fraying of the political coalition sustaining the war effort, a dynamic that historically accelerates pressure for negotiated resolution or drawdown.
outlook: Watch whether the Senate takes up the war powers resolution, the necessary step before it can reach the president's desk.
The key open question is whether Republican defections grow to a two-thirds majority capable of overriding a presidential veto.
Monitor whether the CBO cost projections trigger action in the appropriations process, giving Congress an alternative fiscal lever over the war's continuation.
Track whether growing public opposition ahead of midterm elections translates into electoral consequences for incumbents who voted against the resolution.
